card: Adds UNIX domain socket support to the HTTP RPC server and bitcoin-cli using -rpcbind=unix[:path] and -rpcconnect=unix[:path]. This enables local RPC communication without TCP loopback overhead, relying on filesystem permissions instead of -rpcallowip. The PR also refactors netbase by introducing UnixSocketAddr and SocketAddr, resolving technical debt left from PR #27375. This closes issue #5029, an open feature request since 2014.
changed_since_previous: Rebased onto recent HTTP server changes (including #36159 and #36303), adapting test tracking in interface_http.py to handle connection ID matching and socket buffer limits.
evidence: Closes issue #5029, a long-standing feature request for UNIX domain socket support in bitcoind dating back to 2014.
Eliminates the requirement for -rpcallowip when running solely on local UNIX sockets, allowing OS filesystem permissions to govern socket access.
problem: Local RPC communication currently requires TCP over loopback, which incurs unnecessary networking overhead and forces operators to use IP-based access controls rather than standard filesystem permissions. In addition, earlier UNIX socket support in PR #27375 was confined to the Proxy class, leaving socket abstractions coupled to P2P networking classes.

risk.why: A flaw in socket binding, path resolution, or permissions could break RPC communication or expose the RPC interface to unauthorized local users.

scope_notes: Refactors netbase to introduce SocketAddr and UnixSocketAddr, updating Proxy, HTTPServer, and bitcoin-cli, along with extending the functional test framework (AuthServiceProxy and TestNode) to support UNIX socket connections.
summary: Adds UNIX domain socket support to Bitcoin Core's HTTP server and bitcoin-cli using the -rpcbind=unix and -rpcconnect=unix options (supporting default or custom paths). It introduces UnixSocketAddr and SocketAddr in netbase to abstract generic network endpoints from P2P-specific classes like CService, refactoring Proxy and HTTPServer to use this abstraction. When binding exclusively to UNIX sockets, default TCP loopback listeners are omitted and -rpcallowip is not required.
